orders.text:
MCC No. 5967/12 (Recall Application)
IN
AO No. 295/2012
Hon’ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Mr. Vinay Kumar, Standing Counsel for 
the applicant/State. 
 Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate for 
respondents. 
 Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
 On 17.07.2012, 48 hours time was granted 
to the counsel for the State to remove the 
defects pointed out by the Registry. It was also 
observed in the order that in case, defects are 
not removed within the stipulated time, the 
appeal shall stand dismissed without reference 
to the Bench. In compliance of that order, the 
defects were not removed within the stipulated 
time and the appeal stood dismissed without 
reference of the Bench. 
 Now instant application has been moved 
on behalf of the applicant/State seeking recall 
of the order dated 17.07.2012 on the ground 
that the matter relates to Uttarkashi and decree 
was to be obtained from District Court, 
Dehradun due to which efforts could not be 
made in order to remove the defects. 
 I have perused the order sheet. The 
appeal was filed on 28th June, 2012, thereafter 
time upto 5th July, 2012 was given for removing 
the defects and time was again extended upto 
10.07.2012. When the matter came on board on 
17.01.2012 again time was granted for removing 
the defects. It appears that the applicant/ 
appellant is not, at all, serious in the matter. In 
these circumstance, I was inclined to dismiss 
the recall application, but considering the 
veracity of the matter and in the interest of 
justice, I allow the recall application subject to 
payment of the cost of ` 2,000/-(Rs. Two 
thousand) to be paid to the High Court Legal  Services Committee within a period of one week 
from today. Counsel for the applicant/appellant 
shall produce a copy of receipt in the Registry 
within ten days from today. 
 In case, cost so imposed, is not paid, this 
order shall stand recalled and incase, cost is 
made absolute within the timeframe, the 
appellant is granted time upto 3rd August, 2012 
to remove the defects. Further, in case cost is 
paid and defects are removed, the appeal be 
listed for orders on 4th August, 2012. 
 (V.K. Bist, J.) 
 27.07.2012

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL 
 
 Misc. Application No. 6252 of 2013
In
Appeal from Order No. 295 of 2012
State of Uttarkhand through
Superintendent Engineer, Maneri
Bhali Stage-II Circle, Joshiyara
Uttarkashi
 ….....Defendant/Appellant.
Versus
Ms. Hydel Construction Pvt. Ltd. Dehradun
through Shri Rupinder Singh Thind Director
M/s Hydel Construction Pvt. Ltd. Head
Office at SCO 141-142, Sector -9C
Madhya Marg, Chandigarh in 
Uttarakhand Officer at 49, Race Course
Dehradun 
…............Plaintiff/Respondent
Shri T.A.Khan, Senior Advocate, assisted by Shri I.P.Kohli,
Advocate, present for the appellant. 
Shri V.K.Kohli, Senior Advocate, assisted by Shri H.M. Bhatia,
Advocate, present for the respondent.
Hon’ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
This is Civil Misc. Application No. 6252 of 2013
for release of the amount deposited by the appellant in 2
compliance of order dated 21.08.2012.
(2) Heard.
(3) Brief facts of the case are that a dispute arose
between the appellant (State of Uttarkhand) and the
respondent M/s Hydel Construction Pvt. Ltd. which
was referred to the Arbitral Tribunal. The Arbitral
Tribunal gave its award on 06.02.2011. The present
appellant filed an application under section 34 of
Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, before the
District Judge, Dehradun. After hearing the parties the
application filed under section 34 of said act was
dismissed vide impugned order dated 06.01.2012, and
this appeal was filed on behalf of the State, which was
admitted vide this court's order dated 21.08.2012. This
Court at the time of admitting the appeal directed the
appellant to deposit the entire amount directed to be
paid vide the award passed by the Arbitral Tribunal,
within a period of eight weeks.
(4) Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that
the project of Maneri Bhali phase II after its completion
has already started the generation of electricity, and the
respondents are being deprived of their payment.
(5) Having considered submissions of learned counsel 3
for the appellant, and learned counsel for the
respondent, the Misc. Application 6252 of 2013 is
disposed of, with the direction that 50 % amount of the
deposited by the appellant shall be released in favour of
the respondent. Rest of the 50 % amount is directed to
be deposited in the Fixed Deposits to prevent the loss
of interest of said sum.
(6) List this appeal for final hearing in due course. 
 
(Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt.26.06.2013
